quality_notes: Curious Refuge Labs review scored 8.26/10 overall (listed as 8.29/10 in the benchmark header). Category scores: Prompt Adherence 8.0-8.11/10, Temporal Consistency 8.0-8.11/10, Visual Fidelity 8.4-8.44/10, Motion Quality 8.0/10, Style & Cinematic Realism 7.77/10. Praised for a "physics-first" behavior: strong results (perfect 10/10) appear when shots use geometric anchoring (large high-contrast static elements like bridges, cups, anchored subjects, deep backgrounds with shallow depth of field), explicit single-vector camera moves ("slow push-in", dolly), spatial prepositions and cinematic grammar. Weaknesses: Temporal Consistency collapses in 2D animation (dropped to 3.0-6.0 range) because flat planes lack high-detail anchors/tracking markers, causing subject drift and frame-by-frame re-generation; the physics-first bias sacrifices Prompt Adherence when compute is exhausted to preserve Temporal Consistency, Motion Quality, then Visual Fidelity; human movement auto-triggers pretrained motion maps with no interpretation.
notes: Specs: Max Duration 15s native; Max Resolution up to 4K native; Frame Rate 30-60fps; Native Audio Sync (sound effects + speech generated with video); Motion Control puppeteering tools for high-difficulty physics (fighting, hugging, object interaction). Recommended for AI video artists due to high fidelity ceiling, mathematical predictability and cinematic control. Compared to competitors: Sora 2 has stronger character consistency and prompt logic; Veo 3.1 is less stable/reliable; Runway has superior style-transfer and experimental creative tools. Review by Brian Dalton (Curious Refuge), stated non-biased and unaffiliated with Kling.
